_comment: Pins for the third-party mods the installer downloads. This file is BOTH
embedded in the installer (the always-available fallback) and read from
the repo at install time, so a pin can be refreshed by editing this file
on the main branch — no installer release, no build toolchain.
Editing checklist when an upstream mod updates:
1. Download the new file from its pageUrl by hand.
2. Hash it:  certutil -hashfile <file> SHA256
3. Update sha256, sizeBytes and displayVersion here. Commit to main.
4. Bump 'updated'. Installers in the field pick it up on their next run.
The hashes are load-bearing: the installer downloads these files without
a human in the loop and runs the TSLRCM one elevated, so a mismatch is
refused rather than warned about. Never relax a hash to make a download
work — if a file legitimately changed, re-hash it here. If you cannot
verify it, leave the pin alone: the installer already falls back to a
guided manual download, which is safe because the user fetches the file
themselves and vouches for it.
GitHub-hosted mods pin a commit SHA rather than a file hash. Those do not
rot the same way — a pinned commit stays fetchable as long as the repo
exists — but bump them when you want a newer upstream fix.
Mods published as GitHub RELEASE ASSETS pin tag + asset name + hash. A
tagged asset is effectively immutable, so the hash here is a tamper
check rather than a version check; bump tag, assetName, sha256 and
sizeBytes together when adopting a newer release.

_note: K2CP comes from DeadlyStream, NOT from GitHub. The repo
KOTORCommunityPatches/TSL_Community_Patch is where the recipe is
authored, but the payload is not committed there: at the reference
commit below the whole repo is 13 files and tslpatchdata/ holds only
changes.ini and info.rtf. The 713 files K2CP installs ship in this
archive alone. Fetching from the repo produced an install that
applied the changes.ini edits, silently installed no files, and
reported success.
The commit is kept for provenance only — it matches the archive's
release date (2025-09-26) and is not fetched.
Thematic KOTOR Companions (Sniggles & JCarter426), the KOTOR 1 one.
Author-published GitHub release, so no DeadlyStream scrape and no
redistribution: we fetch the author's own asset at a pinned tag.
The asset is the SPOILER-FREE variant. Both variants carry an
identical tslpatchdata payload; they differ only in the bundled
documentation, where the normal one names characters and their
story arcs to justify each stat change. We never show that document
and our users are typically first-time players, so the variant that
cannot spoil anything is the one worth pinning.
No namespaces.ini: single install option, so no option index.
Thematic KOTOR 2 Companions — same authors, same deal as the KOTOR 1
entry above, including the spoiler-free asset choice.
This one HAS a namespaces.ini with two options. We install index 0
('Standard' — stats and starting equipment only). Index 1 additionally
rewrites one late-game encounter to be considerably harder, which is
not something to hand a blind first-time player unannounced.
